options: A single physical server dedicated to one customer
The billing and access boundary — every resource belongs to exactly one subscription
A free trial that expires after 30 days with no other purpose
A synonym for a resource group
questions.explain: A subscription defines what gets billed for a resource and who's allowed to manage it.

options: A physical datacenter building
A billing boundary that replaces the need for a subscription
A logical container that holds related resources, managed and deleted together
A type of virtual machine
questions.explain: A resource group groups related resources — like a web app's App Service, database, and storage account — so they can be managed as one unit.

questions.q: What happens to the resources inside a resource group when that resource group is deleted?
options: Nothing — resources are never affected by their resource group's status
Every resource inside it is deleted along with it
Only the most recently created resource is deleted
They are automatically moved to a different resource group
questions.explain: Deleting a resource group deletes everything inside it — useful for tearing down a whole test environment in one action, but risky if done by mistake.

questions.q: What three fields does creating a resource group in the Azure Portal actually require?
options: Subscription, a credit card number, and a support ticket
Subscription, resource group name, and region
A pre-existing virtual machine, a domain name, and a password
Nothing — resource groups are created automatically with no input
questions.explain: The Create resource group form asks which subscription it belongs to, a name, and a region for the group's own metadata.

questions.q: How many resource groups can a single resource belong to, and how many subscriptions can a resource group belong to?
options: A resource group can span multiple subscriptions at once
A resource can belong to unlimited resource groups simultaneously
Exactly one resource group, and that resource group belongs to exactly one subscription
Resources and resource groups have no ownership relationship at all
questions.explain: Every resource lives in exactly one resource group, and every resource group lives in exactly one subscription.
